gap: No result ChatGPT got states that ChatGPT's 'middle option', the BLUETTI AC70 at $359, is out of stock at BLUETTI US. Its own page still says to expect a restock in 'Early September', and today is November 13. The same results also don't show that 1,024–1,152 Wh stations cost $459–$499 at the makers' own stores today (EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic $459, BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 $499, BLUETTI AC180 $499), which is less than ChatGPT's $549.99 card for the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2. Anker's own store sells that model for $699.99.
standout_why: The only pages ChatGPT cited are the BLUETTI AC70 product pages (bluettipower.com/products/ac70 and its ?variant URL). They show $359, but the stock line was invisible in ChatGPT's answer, and they say nothing about the other brands. The other results are EcoFlow RIVER 2 Max manuals, an FAQ, a 2023 catalog and a spec PDF. None of them gives a price for a 1 kWh station or says which picks you can actually buy now.
decides: This changes the pick. The 768 Wh 'middle' card can't be bought from BLUETTI today. The in-stock 768 Wh choice is the EcoFlow RIVER 2 Pro at $369, available now. In the 1 kWh class, the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 ($499, 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W, 10 ms UPS, both figures from BLUETTI's listing) and the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic ($459, 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W) cost $50–90 less than ChatGPT's C1000 Gen 2 card and $200–240 less than Anker's own price. Any TV runs fine on 1,800 W. For a small TV, the RIVER 2 Max at $309 (499 Wh) is still correct and in stock.
